items.stem: 当达到市场均衡时，买者是支付愿望 ___ 的人，卖者是成本 ___ 的人。
items.explanation: 在经济学中，把潜在买方对某种商品的支付意愿定义为他愿意为之支付的最高价格。消费者剩余就是消费者愿意支付的最高价格与实际支付价格之差。把某个潜在卖方愿意接受的最低价格称为卖方成本。生产者剩余就是生产者愿意出卖的最低价格与实际成交的价格之差。市场均衡时，消费者剩余与生产者剩余都达到最大。故选 B 项。

items.stem: 消费函数的斜率取决于（）。

options.C: 与可支配收入无关的消费总量
options.D: 与可支配收入相关的消费总量

items.explanation: 消费函数是反映消费支出与影响消费支出的因素之间的函数关系式。消费函数可以表示为 $C=\alpha+\beta Y$。式中，$\alpha$ 为自发消费部分，$\beta$ 为边际消费倾向，$\beta$ 和 Y 的乘积表示收入引致的消费。因此，消费函数的斜率取决于边际消费倾向 $\beta$。故选 A 项。

items.stem: According to this passage, insurance is possible because ___ .

options.A: only a small proportion of the insured suffer loss
options.B: everyone at some time suffers loss

items.explanation:
细节理解题。本题的问题是“根据文意，保险是可行的，原因是 ___ ”。A项，“被保险人中只有一小部分真正蒙受损失”；B项，“所有人都有蒙受损失的时候”；C项，“几乎所有人都蒙受损失”；D项，“只有被保险人蒙受损失”。根据题目中关键词找到主题句：On the other hand, not every house is damaged by fire nor every vessel lost at sea. 解释了不是所有人都会遭受损失，只有一小部分人会遭到厄运，因此保险是切实可行的。故选A项。
细节理解题。本题的问题是 “第一自然段中，短语 the pool of contribution（款项总额）的意思是 ___ 。” A 项，“保险公司支付的款项”；B 项，“管理保险的费用”；C 项，“被保险人支付的款项”；D 项，“每笔保险费的金额”。根据题目中关键词找到主题句：If these persons each put a small sum of money into a pool, there will be enough to meet the needs of the few who do suffer loss. In other words, the losses of the few are met from the contributions of the money. This is the basis of insurance. 短语 “the pool of contribution” 是使用了修辞手法，其实质就是保险费的总和，即被保险人支付的款项。故选 C 项。
细节理解题。本题的问题是“对普通商业风险进行投保是不可行的，原因是 ___ ”。A项，“此类风险所需费用昂贵”；B项，“此类风险不能被准确预估”；C项，“此类风险发生率太高”；D项，“保险费用太高”。根据题目中关键词找到主题句：Not all risks can be covered by insurance. Broadly speaking, the ordinary risks of business and speculation cannot be covered. 主题句中，解释了不能对普通商业风险进行投保的原因是无法预估此类风险，只有在风险可以预估的情况下才能对风险投保。故选B项。
细节推理题。本题的问题是“保险单上有时使用过时词语，原因是 ___ ”。A项，“法庭决定不使用时髦词语”；B项，“它被所有的被保险人广泛接受”；C项，“它使普通人能够轻松理解”；D项，“此类词语的含义已被确定”。根据题目中关键词找到主题句：The wording of policies, particularly in marine insurance, often seems very old-fashioned, but there is a sound reason of this. Over a large number of years, many law cases have been brought to clear up the meanings of doubtful phrases in policies. 主题句中，使用过时词语的原因是此类词语含义清晰，不会引起矛盾。故选D项。
观点态度题。该题询问作者对保险的态度。A项，把保险看作一种赌博，文章并未提及此事，排除；B项，是一种赚快钱的方式，保险并没有此种功能，文章也未提及，排除；C项，有用且必要的，从作者对保险业务的成型到保单的签订，都做了很详细的说明，可以推断作者认为保险是有用的，符合题意；D项，说保险是过时的，是文章中形容一些保单措辞的表达，和保险业无关，排除。根据题目中关键词找到主题句：Insurance is the sharing of risks. Nearly everyone is exposed to risk of some sort. 主题句中，作者明确表示几乎所有人都有可能遭受风险，而保险能够分担风险，因此保险是有用而且必需的。故选 C 项。
细节理解题。本题的问题是“从第一段中，我们能得知反向抵押贷款 ___ ？”A项，“反向抵押贷款本来的预期是帮助老年人留在家里”；B项，“反向抵
押贷款正在将所有的老年人赶出家门”；C项，“反向抵押贷款只欢迎老年人”；D项，“任何老年人都能申请反向抵押贷款”。根据题目中关键词找到主题句：The very loans that are supposed to help seniors stay in their homes are in many cases pushing them out. Reverse mortgages, which allow homeowners 62 or older to borrow money against the value of their homes and not pay it back until they move out or die, have long been said with problems. 可以看出反向抵押贷款的初衷本来是帮助老年人留在家中，但往往结果是使老年人丧失房产。B项“all”，C项“only”，D项“any”，说法都过于绝对。故选A项。
细节理解题。本题的问题是“关于反向抵押贷款的问题正确的说法是？”A项，一些贷款机构不愿意把钱借给老年人，与文章第二段第一句话 Some lenders are aggressively recommending loans to seniors who cannot afford the fees associated with them, without mentioning the property taxes and maintenance. 不符，排除；B项，“借款人无法如预期中归还款项”；C项，“联邦和州监管部门正在制定反对意见”；D项，“一些放款人破产了”。根据题目中关键词发现，本题与第一题主题句相同，可以看出反向抵押贷款的最大问题是借款方老年人无法按时还款，因此可能损失自己的房产。故选B项。

items.stem: The phrase “facing foreclosure” most probably implies ___ .

options.A: the widows are pressured to lose their own names
options.B: the widows may be forced to leave their homes
options.C: the widows have misunderstood the reverse mortgage
options.D: the widows do not know what their long-desired things are

items.explanation:
语义题。本题的问题是 “短语‘facing foreclosure’(面临丧失抵押品赎回权) 最可能暗示 ___ ”。定位文章可知，该短语出现在文章第二段最后一句话：Some widows were pressured not to have their names on the contract, without being told that they could be left facing foreclosure after their husbands died. A 项，“寡妇被强迫舍弃自己本来的名字”；B 项，“寡妇可能被强迫离开自己的家”；C 项，“寡妇误解了反向抵押贷款”；D 项，“寡妇不知道自己长久以来渴望得到的东西是什么”。根据本题主题句可知，在签署反向抵押贷款合同时，一些寡妇没有在合同上签字，因此在丈夫去世后，她们可能会丧失自己的房产。故选 B 项。
细节推断题。本题的问题是 “下列关于消费者金融保护局的新规，哪一项是正确的？” 由题干中的 Consumer Financial Protection Bureau 定位本题主题句：Now, as the vast baby boomer generation is entering retirement and more seniors struggle with declining savings, the newly established Consumer Financial Protection Bureau is working on new rules that could mean better disclosure for consumers and stricter supervision of lenders. 可知：随着大量婴儿潮时代出生的人步入退休阶段，更多的老年人正在努力解决积蓄减少这一困境，新成立的消费者金融保护局开始着手制定新的政策，这一举措可能意味着消费者会拥有更好的知情权，借贷方面面临更为严格的监管。A 项，“新规对放款人有利，对借款人有害”；B 项，“新规能帮助婴儿潮时代出生的老年人省钱”；C 项，“新规能帮助消费者更好地理解反向抵押贷款”；D 项，“新规将对消费者更加严格”。故选 C 项。
猜测词义题。本题的问题是 “反向抵押贷款的 ‘危险信号’ 不包括 ___ ”。red flags 不仅可以表示红旗，还可以指危险信号，由上下文可知，此处即为 “危险信号”。根据主题句：There are many of the same red flags, including explosive growth and the fact that these loans are often advertised aggressively without regarded to suitability. 可知，危险信号包括：explosive growth, advertised aggressively without regarded to suitability，他们涉及到：爆炸性增长、很少考虑适合性及积极不当的营销，只有 B 项反向抵押市场改革是 Lori Swanson 目前的工作内容，不包括在危险信号里。故选 B 项。
语义推断题。本题的问题是“在餐馆的故事中，作者最有可能认为服务生 ___ 。”A项，“愚蠢的”；B项，“礼貌的”；C项，“考虑周到的”；D项，“讨厌的”。根据主题句：Forget the fact that you are with another date and are on a diet that doesn't include burgers. 可知，服务生不考虑顾客的需求，擅自为其安排不合适的约会对象和餐点，顾客会感到餐厅服务员的做法令人讨厌。故选D项。
推理判断题。本题的问题是“作者编造了餐馆里的故事目的是 ___ 。”A 项，“展示一些互联网餐厅提供的良好服务”；B 项，“批评一些餐馆服务差劲”；C 项，“显示互联网收集你的数据的能力”；D 项，“证明互联网有不可思议的力量能改变你的饮食”。根据主题句：To some, this is the restaurant equivalent of the Internet. The Net’s ability to profile you through your visits to and interactions at websites provides marketers with an enormous amount of data on you—some of which you may not want them to have. 可知，作者编造餐馆里的故事目的是为了展示互联网收集你个人信息的能力。故选 C 项。
细节理解题。本题的问题是 “关于 cookie 我们可以了解到什么？”。选择依据是第二段第三句及第四句。A 项，“它由菲尔德夫人创造”；B 项，“它通常在您不知道的情况下收集您的信息”；C 项，“它是访问您计算机所需的硬件”；D 项，“它是最新的技术。”根据主题句：A cookie on the Internet is a computer code sent by the site to your computer—usually without your knowledge. During the entire period of time that you are at the site, the cookie is collecting information about yourself, including where you visit, how long you stay there, and how frequently you return to certain pages. 可知，cookie 在您不知情的情况下收集您的信息。故选 B 项。
细节推理题。本题的问题是 “关于 Alexa 我们可以了解到什么？” A 项，Alexa 是以埃及的一位古代英雄命名的”；B 项，“Alexa 被安装在图书馆里”；C 项，Alexa 可
以提供所有有关历史的必要信息”；D项，“与 cookie 相比，Alexa 可以向营销人员提供更多的数据。”根据主题句：A new system called I-librarian Alexa—named after the legendary third century B.C. library in Alexandria, Egypt—does even more. 可知，和 cookie 相比，Alexa 能够为营销人员提供更多的数据。故选 D 项。

items.stem: Which of the following can best reflect the author’s attitude towards cookies and Alexa?
items.explanation: 观点态度题。本题的问题是 “以下哪一项最能反映作者对于 cookies 和 Alexa 的态度？” 判断依据是文中作者所使用的一些词句，如：usually without your knowledge, sound scary 及最后一句。这些显示了作者对 cookie 和 Alexa 持的态度不是正面的。A 项，“怀疑的”；B 项，“赞成的”；C 项，“欢迎的”；D 项，“乐观的”。根据主题句：Not only do you not get paid for providing the information, you probably don’t even know that you are giving it. 可知，作者对于 cookies 和 Alexa 持怀疑的态度。故选 A 项。

items.stem: According to the first two paragraphs, what will banks in Europe be forced to do?

options.B: To close down the poor services.
options.C: To give up their data monopoly.
options.D: To disclose their sources of profits.

items.explanation: 细节推断题。本题的问题是“根据前两段，欧洲银行被迫做什么？”。从第一段第二句：Banks enjoy a monopoly over data that has helped them get away with poor services and fend off competitors. 可知，银行对数据享有垄断地位，第二段第一句 The rules will compel banks to share data easily with licensed third parties. 说银行不得不与第三方共享数据，可见，银行放弃了他们在数据上的垄断。A 项，“保持客户数据安全”；B 项，“关闭劣质服务”；C 项，“放弃他们的数据垄断”；D 项，“披露他们的利润来源。”故选 C 项。

items.explanation: 细节推断题。本题的问题是“在第二自然段中，有关 PSD2 的影响我们从文中可以推断出什么？”从第二段第二句和第三句 “However, opening up banks, and the data they store, is good for consumers and competition. New providers will be better placed to offer all sorts of innovative services, such as a one-click option to put unspent monthly income into a pension plan.” 可知，竞争中新的服务提供商将更好地提供各种创新服务。A 项，“客户更有可能享受更多创新服务”；B 项，“人们不再去银行存钱了”；C 项，“服务提供商不想与银行合作”；D 项，“人们会得到更多的退休金。” 故选 A 项。

items.stem: Which of the following is true in order to successfully implement PSD2?

options.A: Customers are forced to share their bank data.
options.B: Banks are required to open up their entire operational system.
options.C: Regulators should be both tough and flexible.
options.D: Banks and third parties should be regulated with a light touch.

items.explanation:
细节推断题。本题的问题是“为了成功实施 PSD2，以下哪一项是正确的？”。A 项，“客户被迫分享他们的银行数据”；B 项，“银行被要求开放整个操作系统”；C 项，“监管机构应该既强硬又灵活”；D 项，“银行和第三方应该受到轻微管制。”根据原文最后一段第三句和第四句：“Second, regulator must be very tough both in ensuring that banks open up their infrastructure and in withdrawing the licenses of third parties that break the rules. Third, regulators must also be flexible enough to allow for changes as the market evolves.”可知，监管机构需要既强硬又灵活。故选 C 项。
主旨大意题。本题的问题是“这篇文章的主要内容是什么？”A项，“欧洲监管机构面临的挑战”；B项，“欧洲的一项新规则，让银行走向竞争”；C项，“欧洲有缺陷的银行体系的解决方案”；D项，“客户私人银行数据迫在眉睫的威胁。”根据主题句 The rules will compel banks to share data easily with licensed third parties. Bankers in Europe complain that their profits and customer relationships are under threat. 可知，本文主要讲的是欧洲开放银行竞争新规则。故选 B 项。

Insurance is the sharing of risks. Nearly everyone is exposed to risk of some sort. The house owner, for example, knows that his property can be damaged by fire, the ship owner knows that his vessel may be lost at sea; the breadwinner knows that he may die at an early age and leave his family the poorer. On the other hand, not every house is damaged by fire nor every vessel lost at sea. If these persons each put a small sum of money into a pool, there will be enough to meet the needs of the few who do suffer loss. In other words, the losses of the few are met from the contributions of the money. This is the basis of insurance. Those who pay the contribution are known as “insured” and those who administer the pool of contributions as “insurers”.
Not all risks can be covered by insurance. Broadly speaking, the ordinary risks of business and speculation cannot be covered. The risk that buyers will not buy goods at the prices offered is not of a kind that can be statistically estimated, and risks can only be insured against if they can be so estimated.
The legal basis of all insurance is the “policy”. This is a printed form of contract. It states that in return for the regular payment by the insured of a certain sum of money, called the “premium”, which is usually paid every year, the insurer will pay a sum of money or compensation for loss, if the risk actually happens. The wording of policies, particularly in marine insurance, often seems very old-fashioned, but there is a sound reason of this. Over a large number of years, many law cases have been brought to clear up the meanings of doubtful phrases in policies. The law courts have given these phrases a definite and indisputable meaning, and to avoid future disputes the phrases have continued to be used in polices even when they have passed out of normal use in speech.

The very loans that are supposed to help seniors stay in their homes are in many cases pushing them out. Reverse mortgages, which allow homeowners 62 or older to borrow money against the value of their homes and not pay it back until they move out or die, have long been said with problems. Now, federal and state regulators are documenting new instances of abuse as smaller mortgage brokers, including former sub-prime lenders, flood the market after the recent exit of big banks and as defaults on the loans hit record highs.
Some lenders are aggressively recommending loans to seniors who cannot afford the fees associated with them, without mentioning the property taxes and maintenance. Others are wooing seniors with promises that the loans are free money that can be used to finance their long-desired things, without clearly explaining the risks. Some widows were pressured not to have their names on the contract, without being told that they could be left facing foreclosure after their husbands died.
Now, as the vast baby boomer generation is entering retirement and more seniors struggle with declining savings, the newly established Consumer Financial Protection Bureau is working on new rules that could mean better disclosure for consumers and stricter supervision of lenders. More than 775,000 of such loans are outstanding, according to the federal government.
Concerns about the multi-billion dollar reverse mortgages market echo those raised in the lead-up to the financial crisis when consumers were marketed loans—often carrying hidden risks—that they could not afford. “There are many of the same red flags, including explosive growth and the fact that these loans are often advertised aggressively without regarded to suitability,” sad Lori Swanson, the Minnesota attorney general, who is working on reforming the reverse mortgage market.

Imagine you went to a restaurant with your girlfriend, had a burger, paid with a credit card, and left. The next time you go there, the waiter or waitress, armed with your profile data, greets you with, "Hey Joe, how are you? Mary is over there in the seat you sat last time. Would you like to join her for dinner again?" Then you find out that your burger has been cooked and placed on the table. Forget the fact that you are with another date and are on a diet that doesn't include burgers.
Sound a little bizarre? To some, this is the restaurant equivalent of the Internet. The Net's ability to profile you through your visits to and interactions at websites provides marketers with an enormous amount of data on you—some of which you may not want them to have.
Are you aware that almost every time you access a website you get a “cookie”? Unfortunately, it’s not the Mrs. Field’s recipe. A cookie on the Internet is a computer code sent by the site to your computer—usually without your knowledge. During the entire period of time that you are at the site, the cookie is collecting information about yourself, including where you visit, how long you stay there, and how frequently you return to certain pages.
While this may sound scary enough, cookies aren’t even the latest in technology. A new
system called I-librarian Alexa—named after the legendary third century B.C. library in Alexandria, Egypt—does even more. While cookies track what you are doing at one site. Alexa collects data on all your web activities, such as which site you visit next, how long you stay there, whether you click on advertisements, etc. All this information is available to marketers, who use it to market more effectively to you. Not only do you not get paid for providing the information, you probably don’t even know that you are giving it.

The data a bank has stored on its servers is more valuable than the gold in its vaults. Banks enjoy a monopoly over data that has helped them get away with poor services and fend off competitors. In Europe, at least, that is all about to change with a new set of regulations, named PSD2.
The rules will compel banks to share data easily with licensed third parties. Bankers in
Europe complain that their profits and customer relationships are under threat. However, opening up banks, and the data they store, is good for consumers and competition. New providers will be better placed to offer all sorts of innovative services, such as a one-click option to put unspent monthly income into a pension plan.
Nevertheless, some concerns about PSD2 are legitimate. In particular, it is reasonable to wonder about the privacy and security implications of sensitive financial data being shared with third parties. But banks themselves are hardly invulnerable to cyber attacks (网络攻击). And the solutions that the European regulators propose to deal with these worries look promising. Third parties that want to use bank data will need to convince national regulators that their data defenses are solid and are subject to annual regulatory inspections.
The gap between writing rules and implementing them is always large. First, consent from customers to provide access to their bank data must be gained explicitly, and the purposes of the data use should be clearly explained. Second, regulators must be very tough both in ensuring that banks open up their infrastructure and in withdrawing the licenses of third parties that break the rules. Third, regulators must also be flexible enough to allow for changes as the market evolves. Since the new entrants will not be licensed to engage in riskier financial activities—such as lending money—it makes sense to regulate them with a lighter touch. But if some Fintech providers do end up becoming systemically important, higher standards of oversight might be necessary.
